messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: GPU serving cluster 'pool-west-3' queue growth > 95% for 10m, throttling observed, autoscaler failed to provision additional nodes (reason: max_instances_reached). Severity: P1 (potential customer impact). Runbook: /runbooks/gpu-autoscale.md

oncall-sre: ack. I'm jumping on it, will gather metrics and check autoscaler logs.

sre-jen: I'm on metrics: 95th latency for generate token is spiking to 1.6s and queue length at 2.1k requests. Throttle rate up from 0 to ~28% over last 8m.

infra-lee: looking at autoscaler controller logs — saw repeated scale attempts rejected due to account-level max_instances cap. Also saw api rate limit errors when querying cloud provider.

ml-runtime: suspicious: prefix-cache hit rate dropped from 82% -> 18% around 09:12 UTC, throughput per-GPU dropped accordingly. I see a config change yesterday to continuous batching window and a new prefix_cache_eviction param rolled out via PR #4271.

oncall-sre: can you paste the change?

ml-runtime: here are the relevant snippets from the deploy log:

```
# config applied 2026-03-14T21:05Z
continuous_batching.enabled = true
continuous_batching.window_ms = 20  # previously 8
prefix_cache.max_entries = 20000  # previously 100000
prefix_cache.eviction_policy = "aggressive"
```

ml-runtime: That reduction in prefix_cache.max_entries + aggressive eviction matches the drop in hits. More cache misses -> K/V warmups -> higher per-request token compute -> queue grows.

infra-lee: autoscaler hitting a hard account cap is a separate but compounding issue — we attempted scale but cloud account limit prevented it. Will check if we can request temporary lift.

support-alex: Support reports an uptick in 503/429 from multiple customers in EU region, started ~09:15 UTC. CS is getting complaints from a couple of mid-tier customers.

cs-lead: Noted. Eng please prioritize mitigation. Patch communications to affected customers?

product-sre: adding customer impact tag to this incident. Which routes/models are most impacted?

ml-runtime: models using v2-large-opt and v2-chat-1 are showing highest queue latency — they are the ones with heavy prefix cache dependency (long-system prompts + prefix reuse).

oncall-sre: immediate mitigations proposal: 1) rollback prefix_cache params to previous values (restore max_entries=100000, eviction_policy=default), 2) temporarily reduce continuous_batching.window_ms to 6-8ms, 3) manual scale-up of pool-west-3 nodes if account cap lifted, else failover portion of traffic to pool-west-1 (fallback) and reduce model concurrency.

infra-lee: I can request a temporary increase to account limit but that takes ~15-30m with support. Meanwhile I can force immediate failover by updating routing policy to route 30% of traffic for affected models to pool-west-1. Do we want that?

sre-jen: do both: rollback config now, adjust batching window, and reroute 30% to west-1. We'll run immediate canary after rollback.

deploy-bot: @ml-runtime rolling config rollback job started: revert-configs/2026-03-14--prefixcache-rollback -> in_progress. Job id: rb-5543.

ml-runtime: deploying rollback: applying terraform change to config store and triggering hot-reload on runtime nodes.

deploy-bot: RB-5543: The rollback applied to config-store, pushing updates to 120 runtime pods. Expect 2-3 rolling restarts across pods.

oncall-sre: will monitor metrics. If restarts cause transient failures, we may need to reduce concurrency per pod.

infra-lee: routing update queued: setting route weight v2-large-opt pool-west-1=30%, pool-west-3=70%. Executing now.

deploy-bot: route-update:v2-large-opt -> success. New weights applied.

sre-jen: rollback finished. prefix_cache.max_entries restored. prefix_cache.hit_rate showing initial improvement (now 45% and trending up). Queue length decreased from 2.1k -> ~950 in 6m. Throttle rate down to 12%. Latency improving but still above baseline.

ml-runtime: also reduced continuous_batching.window_ms to 7ms live via runtime control plane. That reduced individual request wait time for batching.

support-alex: seeing 503s drop significantly for customers we raised earlier. CS updated customers and asked them to reopen if they see further errors.

cs-lead: good. Please prepare short customer-facing summary after we stabilize.

infra-lee: cloud support responded: temporary quota increase approved +50 instances for 1h (request id Q-9012). I'll start a manual scale to absorb remaining queue.

noncall-sre: scaling pool-west-3 by +30 GPUs now (manual). Command: `cloudctl compute scale --pool pool-west-3 --add 30 --reason "incident 1957654321"`

deploy-bot: scale job started: scale-7890. Estimated spin-up time 6m.

sre-jen: scale completed, new capacity online. Queue now ~120 and dropping. Throttle ~1-2%. 95th latency returning to baseline.

ml-runtime: confirm prefix_cache hit rate back to ~80% after warm-up. Continuous batching change also reduced extra latency. Both changes combined recovered throughput per-GPU.

product-sre: inventorying customer impact: 7 customers reported errors (2 enterprise, 5 mid-market). We should open follow-up for billing refunds? suggest evaluating token overage and SLA breach windows.

support-alex: logging all affected customers in the incident ticket. CS will coordinate outreach for the 2 enterprise accounts.

noncall-sre: staging handoff notes: cause = config regression (prefix_cache.param change + continuous_batching.window increase) reduced cache efficiency -> increased compute per request -> queue growth. Secondary cause = autoscaler blocked by account hard cap and cloud api rate limits, preventing automated capacity add.

oncall-sre: mitigations applied: 1) rollback prefix_cache params, 2) reduced continuous batching window, 3) temporary traffic reroute to pool-west-1 (30%), 4) requested & received temporary quota increase, 5) manual scale +30 GPUs, 6) started customer comms.

sre-jen: current status: all checks green, queue stable, no new alerts for 12m. Moving to monitoring.

product-sre: prioritizing postmortem. Owner?

noncall-sre: I'll own the postmortem draft and coordinate with ml-runtime and infra. Next steps: root cause analysis to include timeline, why prefix_cache change shipped (PR review notes), add automated pre-deploy canary for cache-hit regression, create autoscaler circuit-breaker to detect quota-limit failures and trigger fallback routing automatically.

ml-runtime: will add a deploy-time gate that blocks prefix_cache reductions >20% without a benchmark run (simulated workload). Also add continuous-batching AB test to monitor latency vs throughput tradeoffs.

infra-lee: will make autoscaler more resilient to cloud api ratelimits: add jittered retries and backoff; also implement a fallback to route traffic before it reaches critical queue size if scale requests are repeatedly failing.

cs-lead: CS will prepare customer-impact summary, template for outreach and any credits/refunds.

support-alex: document saved to incident ticket IT-1957654321. Will attach logs and affected customer list.

oncall-sre: handing off to next oncall @sre-jen in 30m. Current severity-> P2 for follow-up work; Core mitigation complete. If anyone sees queue > 300 or throttle > 10% reopen P1.

sre-jen: taking handoff. Will monitor for 2h and coordinate postmortem.

product-sre: tagging this incident for retro and capturing action items.

incident-bot: AUTOMATED NOTE: Pager acknowledged by oncall-sre at 2026-03-15T09:22:15Z. Incident marked mitigated at 2026-03-15T09:44:01Z.

sre-jen: quick summary for postmortem: timeline, why config change slipped through (lack of perf gate), autoscaler failure mode (quota + ratelimit), mitigations, customer impact, follow-ups. I'll create the PM and link to the postmortem doc.

cs-lead: thanks all.

support-alex: closing support updates unless we hear back from customers.

noncall-sre: final checklist for handoff: attach metrics dashboard snapshot, attach deploy logs (rb-5543), autoscaler logs, cloud quota approval email, list of affected customers. Tagging assignees: ml-runtime (perf gate), infra-lee (autoscaler backoff + fallback), oncall-sre (postmortem owner).

sre-jen: noted. I'll add the runbook improvements to the incident ticket.

product-sre: leaving a retrospective note to evaluate whether we should have automated cache-hit health checks and pre-deploy synthetic load tests.

incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED: No new messages for 30m.
